newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt broker sacked for pricing irregularities.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt broker sacked for pricing irregularities.

text.p: An official broker on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange has been dismissed for "serious irregularities" regarding the pricing of shares, the bourse supervisory authority for the state of Hesse said on Thursday.
"The broker failed to process investors' orders in a timely fashion and fabricated transactions to conceal this," said Matthias Kurth, state secretary in Hesse's economics ministry.
The dismissal on June 30 was necessary to protect investors and safeguard the reputation of Germany's financial centre, Frankfurt, Kurth said.
The broker was not accused of a criminal offence because he had not sought personal gain or to harm a third party.

But his infringement of bourse regulations was so severe that the authority was forced to sack him immediately, Kurth said. Kurth declined to say which shares had been affected by the pricing irregularities.
The dismissal followed an investigation in recent weeks.
